Have you ever disappeared from someone's life?

Yep, I finished high school a few months ago and stopped talking to all the friends I made over the past six years except one. Mainly because I was getting sick of them and they were getting sick of me.

I can relate to this so well. I wouldn't call people I knew in back in high school "friends" but they weren't acquaintances either. They were in the awkward middle and it was the lack of intimacy that made it easier for me to move on. Looking back at it now, we had nothing in common and they could be downright assholes to me sometimes. I might sound a bit harsh but I don't miss them at all.

If you're stuck in a building with the same people five times a week for the majority of the year, you're GOING to make friends. Realizing that they're temporary is part of it, and any true friends you've made WILL stick around, regardless if it's work, high school, the waiting room, etc.
I talked to some guy working in a store someplace in America. Then I left and never talked to him again. It was like 10pm and I bought snacks.

There was a guy I started dating when I was around 15. We went steady for a little over a year and then I broke up with him. Over the next 5 or 6 years he always hung around to be the friend that comforted me when I was down and was a really good friend to me. The problem was he never stood up for himself and would constantly let me walk all over him. Once I realized what I was doing and how I was treating him I tried talking to him about it. His reply was, "I just want you to be happy. It doesn't really matter how I feel." That was when it finally clicked that he was so stuck on me that he couldn't see anything else. I told him thanks for being such a good friend, but we need to say good-bye. I told him that if he ever needed me I would be there for him. Then I left. I never called him or messaged him after that. I like to think that I did the right thing.

Yeah, I met a really nice guy online (probably my first mistake), and after spending the night together, we added each other on Facebook. We hung out again, but work called and said they needed me, so we didn't do anything. Every once in a while, he'd post on Facebook about his depression and rough times. I'd text him saying if he needed to talk to someone, he could talk to me. He just said he wanted to be left alone for a bit. What the fuck?! If you're going to be posting stuff like that on Facebook, but turn people (or maybe just me?) away, that's really inconsiderate. After the third time, I unfriended him and stopped following him in Instagram. I don't need that weird drama in my life.

I was in a really seriouse relationship for three years that ended around 2 years ago. I stopped growing as a person, and our relationship became stagnant. She ended up leaving me, but we remained friends (kinda) because we were really close. Which turned out to be torture. I fought tooth and nail trying to get her back, but wasn't interested in me. I ended up cutting her off, cold turkey, so I could begin the process of healing. Havnt spoken to her since. She's tried to contact me in those 2 years since, but I get a weird satisfaction from not responding. Maybe because 2 years ago I would have folded like tissue paper? Idk.
